title: Module Review Quiz: Operators & Expressions (CPP_119 to CPP_126)

slides.title: Operators & Expressions Overview
slides.prompt: This Module Quiz covers arithmetic, relational, logical, assignment, bitwise, increment/decrement operators, and expression evaluation in C++ (CPP_119 to CPP_126).

slides.title: Modulus Operator (CPP_119)
slides.prompt: Fill in the operator used to get the remainder of an integer division.

slides.title: Pre-increment vs Post-increment (CPP_120)
slides.prompt: What will be printed by the following code: int x = 5; cout << ++x;

slides.title: Post-increment Operator (CPP_120)
slides.prompt: Fill in the operator that increments the value after evaluating the current expression.
slides.codeSnippet:
int a = 5;
int b = a___; // b gets 5, then a becomes 6

slides.title: Relational Operators (CPP_121)
slides.prompt: Which operator is used to check if two values are equal in C++?

slides.title: Not Equal Operator (CPP_121)
slides.prompt: Fill in the correct operator to test if two variables are NOT equal.

slides.title: Logical AND Operator (CPP_122)
slides.prompt: Which operator evaluates to 'true' only if BOTH operands are true?

slides.title: Logical OR Operator (CPP_122)
slides.prompt: Fill in the logical operator that yields true if AT LEAST ONE condition is true.

slides.title: Compound Assignment (CPP_123)
slides.prompt: What is the equivalent shorthand for 'x = x + 5'?

slides.title: Ternary Operator (CPP_124)
slides.prompt: Fill in the missing symbol in the conditional (ternary) operator.

slides.title: Operator Precedence (CPP_125)
slides.prompt: What is the result of the expression: 10 + 2 * 5 ?

slides.title: Bitwise AND (CPP_126)
slides.prompt: Fill in the single bitwise operator that performs a bitwise AND operation.

slides.title: Bitwise Left Shift (CPP_126)
slides.prompt: What does shifting an integer to the left by 1 bit (x << 1) usually accomplish mathematically?

slides.title: Logical NOT Operator (CPP_122)
slides.prompt: Fill in the operator used to reverse the logical state of its operand.
